position.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the South Division block bounded by South Water, Wells, Lake and Franklin; standing ON the South Water Street frontage itself, one unit of the party-line row along it
position.note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_south_water_franklin, the block's South Water Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its east wall is fixed by the east end of the run's own frontage, 1.5 m clear of the side lot line at that end. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at South Water Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.value: J. H. Mulford — watches, jewelry, engravings and fancy goods
occupants.note: SEATED BY THE STREET-FACE ADOPTION POLICY (docs/STREET-FACE-ADOPTION.md, the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 for T-0354, extended 2026-08-30 for T-0416; liberty L212). The newspaper register places this business on South Water Street AND NOTHING NARROWER — 5 printings, 1834-06-04 to 1835-08-12, claims chicago_democrat_1834_06_04#c004, chicago_democrat_1834_07_02#c022, chicago_democrat_1834_07_09#c023, chicago_democrat_1834_12_03#c012, chicago_democrat_1835_08_12#c013 — so it takes the STREET FACE and not a lot. THE ROOF'S PLATTED LOT FACES South Water Street, which is the plat's own answer to which street it fronts. WHICH roof on that face it is given is an allocation by tools/adopt_street_faces.py and not a reading of any source, and nothing here says this business stood nearer the corner than any other on the same face. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption: the business is documented, the building under it is not, and this attribute is graded `reconstructed` because the invented part is the whole of the placement.

frontage.why: T-0430, the second deal on this block, and the SECOND of the four South Water blocks T-0009's ruling unblocked — blk_south_water_lasalle took its own second deal first, on 2026-08-30 under T-0429, and the reading below is that run's reading applied to different ground rather than a new one. THE FACE IS NOT RE-ARGUED: this block's north face is South Water Street, the town's business front, and the committed hierarchy in data/streets/1835.json grades it `principal`. What was in doubt until that ruling is whether the LINE would move — T-0143 and T-0188 each refused to tighten a party-line row against a street line that might, and T-0317 inherited the refusal. T-0009 closed it: the corridor was re-derived from committed control (`recentred`, +8.58 m) and data/streets/1835.json was not touched, so the drawn line does not move. THE ROW STILL STANDS ON THE BLOCK FACE AND NOT ON THAT CORRIDOR, which is the distinction the two refusals were protecting: the face is committed geometry read from data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the run takes its line, its bearing and the end it packs back from off that boundary. The 8.58 m the corridor moved is therefore not in this placement at all, and if the strip between the corridor and the block faces is later resolved (T-0419) these roofs do not move with it. THE LOT IS THE ONE THE SCHEDULE COUNTS FREE, AND IT TOOK A LEDGER REPAIR TO REACH IT. tools/reconcile_665.py derives this block at 11 standing roofs, 2 free lots and 4 of headroom; the free lots are 1 and 2, read by tools/plat_occupancy.py's `exclusive_lots` from what actually stands. Lot 1 is the Lake-and-Franklin corner on the back tier and stays open. Lot 2 is this block's one free lot of business frontage — and the first entry above had RESERVED it by naming lots 2, 4 and 6 as the frontage its run was dealt, when the run it built stands on lot 6 alone. That entry now names lots 4 and 6 — lot 4 because its own privy stands in that lot's yard, lot 6 because that is where its roofs are — and lot 2, which nothing it wrote has ever stood on, comes off the list. The correction moves no record and is set out in its own `why`. THE CORNER CLAUSE DOES NOT BIND HERE and is not invoked: lot 0 is the Franklin corner and lot 6 the Wells corner, both built on, so lot 2 is an interior lot of this face and there is no corner for a run to be built to. THE END RULE IS READ RATHER THAN ASSERTED — tools/measure_end_rule.py reads this face at a spread of 73.22 m and a unit step of 6.07 m under the walked criterion, which is above the 6.00 m floor, so a grading is admissible here; the walk from lot 2's frontage to the Dearborn drawbridge's south abutment is 453.19 m against lot 4's 428.78 m and lot 6's 404.36 m, so the better end of this face, and of this lot, is the EAST. The run is anchored there and packs west. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, lot 2's own stretch of it and the end the run packs back from are all read from the committed block boundary, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage. The row adopts the setback the three roofs already standing on this face were built to, so the street wall of blk_south_water_franklin stays one wall.
